messages:
alex: quick heads-up: ran into flakiness in the python async lib when stress-testing client-side throttling. observed bursts of 429s even though quota headers indicated tokens available.

priya: can you paste a small trace? is this on the latest release branch?

alex: yep on main. trace below (trimmed):

```
REQUEST -> POST /v1/generate
Client-now: 2025-11-03T12:10:01.123Z
bucket_before: 1
RESPONSE <- 200
X-Redwood-Quota-Limit: 120
x-redwood-quota-remaining: 0
x-redwood-quota-reset: 1760000000
RETRY -> 429 on next request
```

alex: interesting bit is server returned remaining=0 but our client immediately tried another request because in-memory bucket still held 1.

nate: probably two coros: coro A reads bucket=1, yields at await, coro B also reads bucket=1, both decrement locally, send. A gets 200 updates headers->0, B gets 429. classic read-modify-write race.

irina: we already have a _token_bucket in sync client that uses threading.Lock. async client used an atomic int w/out lock for perf. seems that's the culprit.

priya: performance concern: adding a global asyncio.Lock around every acquire could become a bottleneck for high qps. alternatives?

nate: consider per-client asyncio.Lock but only around header-update and acquire read-modify-write. Acquire path can do a fast optimistic check and if it would go negative then take the lock and re-check. so most fast-paths avoid the lock.

irina: that sounds good. pseudocode suggestion:

```
# fast path
if self._bucket.try_consume():
    return
# slow path
async with self._bucket_lock:
    if not self._bucket.try_consume():
        await self._wait_for_tokens()
```

alex: also encountering header name inconsistencies: some customers/proxies lower-case vendor headers. our parser used exact-case keys in one place and lower() in another. we should canonicalize to lower() everywhere when reading.

qa-bot: repro steps I used: spawn 40 coros hitting the client with small token-cost ops, set quota to 2 per second on server side. intermittent failure rate ~3%. captured proxied responses where headers were removed entirely on 429s.

priya: when headers are missing on 429 we must prefer Retry-After if present and fall back to exponential backoff. also emit a metric 'quota.header.missing' so ops can see pattern.

nate: about the client-side throttler utility: we currently expose RedwoodThrottle class in experimental package. need API parity between sync/async and clearer semantics: acquire(timeout=None) for sync, async acquire(timeout=None) for async. and instrument with metrics: tokens_consumed, tokens_refilled, header_parse_errors.

irina: typing/pyright notes: annotate lock as Optional[asyncio.Lock] in __init__ = None and create on first use to avoid event-loop creation in import-time. add TYPE_CHECKING guards if needed.

alex: good point. got burned once creating loop-bound primitives at import. add test that imports module at top-level (no loop) to ensure no loop creation.

priya: tests: unit test for concurrent acquires asserting only N proceed when remaining=N. integration test with tiny proxy that lowercases headers and strips them on 429 to ensure fallbacks hit. add flake-tolerant timing assertions.

qa-bot: I'll add the proxy-based integration test to the qa harness. tagging @irina for test details.

nate: small API nit: make Retry-After parsing accept seconds OR HTTP-date formats, and if reset header present prefer it to Retry-After. also round up windows to avoid zero-length waits.

irina: document in changelog the parity changes, callout: sync/async throttle semantics now match and shared parser util introduced. bump minor version for experimental package.

alex: I'll draft a PR with: - shared header parser util - optimistic fast-path + lock slow-path - metrics for header parse / missing headers - tests + docs. cc @priya @nate for review.

ci-bot: queued test run for PR #4599  unit(38) integration(4) flake(2)

priya: great. one follow-up: can we expose a debug mode that logs token-bucket ops per-request to help customers debug throttling behavior in staging? probably opt-in via client config.

alex: yes, adding client.debug_throttling boolean that toggles verbose logs. will include in PR. thanks all :rocket:
